correctness.rationale: For every n>=2 and 1<=k<n, the exact law q_{n,k}(l)=k*l*C_{l-1}*Z(n-l,k-1)/(n*Z(n,k)) follows by Catalan primitive-excursion enumeration and size-biasing by the chosen two-step cell. Z(m,j)=j/(2m-j)*binom(2m-j,m-j). The consecutive-k likelihood ratio is proportional to k/(k-1)*(m-k+1)/(2m-k), m=n-l, increasing in m for k>=3 and constant when k=2; finite support loss makes adjacent laws distinct, and k=1 is a top-atom boundary. The conditional fair excursion signs give Var(A|K=k)=n/4 E[L*|K=k], strictly decreasing from n^2/4 to n/4. For k/n->rho in (0,1), recurrence q(1) plus uniform subcritical geometric bounds on ratios gives the claimed q_rho and first-moment convergence. Checks: independently enumerated every balanced 2n-step bridge n<=7, giving 140 exact cell-size probabilities and strict mean monotonicity.
